breakNotes.October Student Break: On Plano ISD's graphic calendar, October 12–14 are student/teacher holidays, October 15 is a staff day/student holiday, and October 16 is a Campus PLC day/student holiday. “October Student Break” is our student-facing label for the five-day no-school window.
breakNotes.Thanksgiving Break: Students have no classes all five weekdays. Plano ISD's text-format calendar labels November 23–27 as Thanksgiving Break, while the graphic calendar lists November 23–24 as Professional Learning Trade Days and November 25–27 as Thanksgiving Break. Classes resume Monday, November 30.
breakNotes.Winter Break: The official Winter Break ends January 1. January 4 is a separate student holiday and staff day; classes resume Tuesday, January 5.
breakNotes.Spring Break: Classes resume Monday, March 22. Additional student days off follow on March 26 and March 29.

calendarFaqs.q: When does Plano ISD start school in 2026–27?
calendarFaqs.a: The first day of classes is Tuesday, August 11, 2026.

calendarFaqs.q: When is the last day of school for Plano ISD in 2026–27?
calendarFaqs.a: The last day of classes is Friday, May 21, 2027. It is also an early-release day and the end of the fourth grading period.

calendarFaqs.q: When is Plano ISD Spring Break in 2027?
calendarFaqs.a: Spring Break runs Monday, March 15, through Friday, March 19, 2027. Classes resume Monday, March 22.

calendarFaqs.q: When is Plano ISD Winter Break in 2026–27?
calendarFaqs.a: Plano ISD officially lists Winter Break from Monday, December 21, 2026, through Friday, January 1, 2027. January 4 is a separate student holiday and staff day.

calendarFaqs.q: Are Plano ISD students off October 12–16, 2026?
calendarFaqs.a: Yes. Students have no classes from Monday, October 12, through Friday, October 16. Plano ISD's graphic calendar labels October 12–14 as student/teacher holidays, October 15 as a staff day/student holiday, and October 16 as a Campus PLC day/student holiday.

calendarFaqs.q: When do Plano ISD students return after Winter Break?
calendarFaqs.a: Classes resume Tuesday, January 5, 2027, which is also the start of the second semester.

calendarFaqs.q: Is May 21, 2027 an early-release day in Plano ISD?
calendarFaqs.a: Yes. Friday, May 21 is the last day of classes, an early-release day, and the end of the fourth grading period.

customSections.label: Calendar Details That Are Easy to Miss
customSections.content: Plano ISD publishes both a graphic calendar and a text-format academic calendar. They agree on when students attend school, but a few staff-day labels differ. The notes below explain the student-facing schedule and flag those differences where relevant.

definitions.description: Students have no classes for five weekdays. Both calendars list October 12–14 as student/teacher holidays. The text-format calendar groups October 15–16 as student holidays with staff development/work days; the graphic calendar labels October 15 a staff day and October 16 a Campus PLC day.
This is an early-release day, the last day of the first semester, and the end of the second grading period.
Students remain off, but Plano ISD lists this as a student holiday and staff development/work day rather than part of Winter Break. Classes resume January 5.

Students have two consecutive weekdays without classes. The text-format calendar groups February 15–16 as student holidays with staff development/work days; the graphic calendar labels February 15 a staff day and February 16 a Campus PLC day.
These are additional student days off after Spring Break: March 26 is a student/teacher holiday, and March 29 is a student holiday and staff day.

customSections.label: Early Release, Semesters, and Grading Periods
customSections.content: Plano ISD's text-format calendar also provides semester totals, grading-period dates, and published dismissal times.

definitions.description: December 18 and May 21 are early-release days. December 18 closes the first semester; May 21 is the last day of classes.
The first semester has 82 instructional days and the second has 89, for 171 total instructional days.
The four grading periods end October 9, December 18, March 12, and May 21 and contain 43, 39, 46, and 43 instructional days.

The calendar lists 1:10 p.m. exam dismissal for high and senior high schools, 1:30 p.m. for Academy High School, and 12:40 p.m. for middle schools on the last exam day only. Elementary early release is noon; early childhood early release is 11:55 a.m.

sourceReviewDetails: We reconciled every student-impact date across the official text-format and graphic calendars. They agree on student attendance, while staff-day labels differ on October 15–16, November 23–24, and February 15–16.
We also checked semester totals, grading-period lengths, early-release dates, and the dismissal times printed on the text-format calendar.
